aspects.says: An exception thrown inside a catch block leaves the whole try statement; the catch clauses below it never see it.
basis: section:An Exception Thrown in a Catch Block Leaves the Whole try Statement

aspects.says: Catch clauses are tried top to bottom and the first whose type matches runs; a clause below one for its supertype is a compile error.
basis: section:The First Catch Clause That Matches Wins, So a Subclass Goes Above Its Superclass

aspects.says: An instanceof chain inside one broad catch gets no ordering check, so a general test placed first hides the specific branch.
basis: section:The First Catch Clause That Matches Wins, So a Subclass Goes Above Its Superclass
aspects.reason: a dead branch has no observable output a test can tell from a missing branch; the page shows the run, and the label-booking practice grades handler choice at run time

aspects.says: A multi-catch's alternatives must be unrelated, its parameter is implicitly final, and its static type is the alternatives' least upper bound.
basis: section:A Multi-Catch Shares One Handler; Its Parameter Is Final and Typed as What the Types Share

aspects.says: A catch for a checked exception the try block can't throw is a compile error, while Exception, Throwable and unchecked types always compile.
basis: section:A Catch for a Checked Exception the Try Can't Throw Is an Error, Except for Exception and Throwable

aspects.says: Rethrowing an effectively final catch (Exception e) parameter throws only the checked exceptions the try block can throw, so the method keeps its precise throws clause and the caller sees the same exception.
basis: section:Catching Exception to Rethrow It Keeps the Precise throws Clause

aspects.says: Assigning to the catch parameter before throw e makes the compiler treat it as its declared type, Exception.
basis: section:Catching Exception to Rethrow It Keeps the Precise throws Clause
